overall: Claude reviewed 7d4c08b..cefc2ea read-only from a git-archive scratch tree. It reproduced the delegation suites at 126 passed/1 skipped, the full adapter suite at 244 passed/2 skipped, and the legacy suite at 548 passed/6 skipped. Direct probes confirmed 8-process contention, exact schema-v2 refusal, reserved repair markers, mutation-free nonexistent-store reads, crash-replayable repair, honest unauthenticated controller assertions, and deterministic LF-only scaffold-bundle output. The 13 hook-runtime failures in the separate verifier were classified as an out-of-range py-launcher dependency, and the unchanged descendant-cleanup failure as a separate timing-sensitive runner issue. No candidate-specific blocker was found. This is code convergence only, not release authorization.
gaps: The 10,000-record bound is nominal rather than operationally reachable because append re-reads and re-verifies the whole ledger. Claude measured the same quadratic curve on the base and candidate, with a larger schema-v2 constant factor. The practical ceiling is not documented.
If the sidecar lock is absent, a read proceeds unlocked. A race with an append fails closed as apparent corruption rather than accepting a torn record, but can produce a spurious corruption report.
The read lock opens the sidecar with r+b. Ledger reads are mutation-free, but operation on a genuinely write-denied filesystem was not verified.
risks: The unchanged Windows hook definition requires the py launcher; a host without it loses hook runtime with a failure signature that resembles a code defect.
repair_torn_tail exposes a bounded keyword-only fault-injection seam in production code for deterministic crash tests.
A valid ledger report is tamper-evident for observed in-chain changes, not authenticated or suffix-complete attestation.
The adversarial repair corpus is deterministic rather than fuzz or property-testing coverage.
Claude reviewed an extracted candidate tree; a later integrated checkout still requires its own final verification.
